newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Waigel says Italy, France to make more EMU effort.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says Italy, France to make more EMU effort.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel, speaking after EU finance ministers approved Italy's convergence programme, said on Monday Italy and France were prepared to take more steps as needed to reach the budget targets for economic and monetary union.
Germany itself will meet the deficit criterion of 3.0 percent of gross domestic product, Waigel said.
Despite new jobs measures announced by France, Paris has not put the deficit targets in question, he told reporters.
In the convergence programme presented today Italy projects a deficit of 3.0 percent of GDP this year, falling to 1.8 percent in 2000, Waigel said.
"Italy and France are prepared to take more steps to reach the targets," Waigel said.
Asked how he evaluated Italy's chances of reaching the targets, Waigel said "We are still in the middle of the year. Why shouldn't one have the chance to reach a successful conclusion."
On Germany's efforts to meet the 3.0 percent deficit rule Waigel said "We will reach the figure in the treaty, in the protocol."
On European efforts to create jobs Waigel said much could be done without costly new programmes. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
